I think a better analogy would be a cell phone. You normally start the day off with a full battery. However, every now and then your body has to open this app that runs in the background.. you know the kinds, the ones that drain your battery faster than normal. For me, the app is autoimmune. Every now and then, AI will turn on location services... there goes my battery even faster. When it gets really bad, it will turn on vibrations and make the fact that it is draining my battery painfully obvious.

So what do you do when you are no where near a charger and you have this app eating away at your battery? You turn off non-essential apps. I don't play on Facebook, I don't browse the internet excessively. Sure, it may seem like I am being a little less social but to those that are physically around me, I am OK. Sometimes they notice my phone vibrating, and I explain.

And yea, you might need to get to a charger before bedtime. But at least during the day, I was able to do what I can to keep my battery alive. What I don't do is decide that I need to stay attached to a charger or continuously bother those around me to plug in my charger while I surf Facebook.
